name: multiple sclerosis overview
title: Multiple sclerosis: a relapse is new neurological dysfunction lasting 24 hours or more with no other cause; the typical relapses are myelitis, optic neuritis and brainstem or cerebellar syndromes; the diagnosis needs dissemination in space and time on MRI, with CSF oligoclonal bands able to stand in for time, once better explanations are ruled out; treatment is disease-modifying therapy by category plus symptomatic therapy

root.title: Could it be MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS (MS)?
lines: an immune attack (B and T cells) on central nervous system myelin (oligodendrocytes) → axonal damage, then loss
most common disabling neurological disease of young adults in Canada (240 per 100,000) · women 3:1 · age 20-40 · white, Northern European
risk: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV, 32-fold: necessary, NOT sufficient) · genes explain 20-30% · adolescent obesity · smoking · diet · low vitamin D or sunlight · shift work
lesions: cortical or juxtacortical · periventricular · brainstem · cerebellum · spinal cord

groups.title: A RELAPSE: which kind?
lines: NEW neurological symptoms · acute or subacute onset · lasting 24 HOURS or more · no other cause · not a pseudo-relapse
other features: sensory disturbances · fatigue · Lhermitte's sign (an electric shock down the back on bending the neck)

head: h
Myelitis
spinal cord lesion · about 50% at onset
h
Brainstem or cerebellar syndrome
about 15% at onset
clue: case: man in his 20s · vertigo, nausea, some double vision

rows: plain
MRI is central · lumbar puncture supports
2017 McDonald criteria: clinical attacks + MRI or CSF findings, combined
warn
Disseminated in SPACE
lesions in 2 or more typical regions:
• periventricular · cortical or juxtacortical
• infratentorial · spinal cord
warn
Disseminated in TIME
• a NEW lesion on follow-up MRI
• OR enhancing + non-enhancing lesions at once
• CSF oligoclonal bands can stand in for time
bad
ALWAYS rule out a better explanation
neuromyelitis optica (NMO) · myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein disease (MOGAD) · vascular · infection · metabolic (B12)
plain
Course: clinically isolated syndrome → relapsing-remitting (85% at onset) → secondary progressive · or primary progressive from the start
each labelled active or not, progressing or not · score disability on the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS, 0-10)
prognosis: 50% minor disability at 6-8 y · 21% need a walking aid at 15 y · median 27.9 y (age 59) to need one
ok
Disease-modifying therapy: think in CATEGORIES
• injectable platforms: interferons, glatiramer (Copaxone) · long-term safety data, LOW adherence
• standard orals: dimethyl fumarate, teriflunomide, fingolimod · easier than injections
• induction: cladribine · oral, effect lasts ~4 y
• high efficacy: natalizumab, B-cell therapies (ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, rituximab) · B-cell therapies now very common
ok
Treat the symptoms too
• spasticity: baclofen, tizanidine, stretching, physiotherapy
• pain, tingling: amitriptyline, gabapentin, duloxetine, CBD
• bladder: solifenacin, urology referral · erections: sildenafil
• depression: antidepressants
• fatigue: amantadine, modafinil · walking: fampridine

panels.title: Differential: VITAMIN
items: V vascular: migraine, stroke, CADASIL · I infection: HIV, syphilis, Lyme, West Nile
T toxins: cocaine, additives · A autoimmune: NMO, MOG · Sjögren's, Behçet's
M metabolic: B12 · I inflammatory: sarcoid · N neoplastic: lymphoma
top differential, how common: MS 1500 · NMOSD 30 · MOGAD 30 · sarcoid 15 · lymphoma 6 · ADEM 3 · Sjögren's 2
